Article.ArticleTitle: RAD51C/XRCC3 facilitates mitochondrial DNA replication and maintains integrity of the mitochondrial genome.

Abstract.AbstractText: Mechanisms underlying mitochondrial genome maintenance have recently gained wide attention as mutations in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) lead to inherited muscular and neurological diseases which are linked to aging. It has been previously reported that human RAD51, RAD51C and XRCC3 localize to mitochondria upon oxidative stress and are required for the maintenance of mtDNA stability. Since RAD51 and RAD51 paralogs are spontaneously imported into mitochondria, their precise role in mtDNA maintenance during unperturbed conditions remains elusive. Here, we show RAD51C/XRCC3 as an additional component of mitochondrial nucleoid having nuclear independent roles in mtDNA maintenance. RAD51C/XRCC3 localizes to the mtDNA regulatory regions in D-loop along with the mitochondrial polymerase POLG, and this recruitment is dependent upon Twinkle helicase. Moreover, upon replication stress, they are further enriched at the mtDNA mutation hotspot Region D310. Notably, absence of RAD51C/XRCC3 affects the stability of POLG on mtDNA. As a consequence, RAD51C/XRCC3 deficient cells exhibit reduced mtDNA synthesis and increased lesions in the mitochondrial genome leading to overall unhealthy mitochondria. Together, these findings propose a mechanism for a direct role of RAD51C/XRCC3 in maintaining the mtDNA integrity under replication stress conditions.
